paper_title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $τ^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $τ^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $τ^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Large Language Model (LLM) agents competence depends on how it connects reasoning, action, and observation. Mathematical assistants may call python interpreter (Xue et al., 2026) to calculate or directly derive an answer; Service agents may query an account or request missing identifier. Reasoning and Acting (ReAct) (Yao et al., 2022), which interleaves reasoning traces with task-specific actions, allowing an LLM to plan, track its progress, and handle exceptions through thought while gathering information from external environments such as search APIs or tools, decouples reasoning with actions and observations and becomes the most widely-used paradigm (Schick et al., 2023; Qin et al., 2024) which LLMs use to solve agentic tasks (Jimenez et al., 2024; Wei et al., 2025). On-Policy Distillation (OPD), which transfers teacher capabilities by supervising trajectories sampled by the student (Agarwal et al., 2024; Song and Zheng, 2026), has also become an important step in LLM post-training pipeline (Ma et al., 2026; Team et al., 2026; Xu et al., 2026). OPD training can affect models choices, especially in the multi-turn agentic tasks, including how to organize reasoning and tool-use, how to obtain new information, interact with the environment, and so on. We study these ReAct interaction patterns across four domains: (1) pure natural-language general reasoning (Hendrycks et al., 2021) (GR), (2) general reasoning with code-interpreter tools (He-Yueya et al., 2023; Qian et al., 2025) (CI), (3) ALFWorld (Shridhar et al., 2021), and (4) τ 2-bench (Barres et al., 2025). We find two observable ReAct pattern shifts in trajectories of the above agentic tasks. First, OPD can shift the route to mathematical answer between tool-assisted computation and direct natural-language reasoning ( 4.1): GR-domain OPD training starkly reduces models tool attempt rate from 70.4% to 14.4% in the CI tasks. Second, it can change how the student chooses actions, adjusts them after environment feedback, and waits for information or authorization before acting ( 4.2): CI supervision improves both ALFWorld and τ 2 tasks, accompanied by fewer repeated actions and more complete queries. Meanwhile, we find that ALFWorld-domain OPD makes students τ 2 performance drastically drop from 41.5% to 6.6%. The student frequently generates request-like text alongside tool calls without yielding the turn to the user. More importantly, semantic review identifies calls that depend on unavailable user information or authorization in 55.8% of trajectories. These findings connect cross-domain outcomes to reasoning 1 routes, feedback-driven actions, and the acquisition of observations. We analyze that severely overfitting to task-specific ReAct patterns is the main cause of the observed negative transfer. Hence, we design selective policy ( 5.1), which keeps the generic agentic abilities (mostly derived from the agentic RL training (Yu et al., 2025)) and discards the plain transfer of surfacelevel task-specific ReAct patterns, as illustrated in Figure 1. Given students rollout, we use both of the teachers checkpoints before and after domainspecific RL to compute token log-probabilities for sampled tokens. Naturally, the difference () of loglikelihood between two checkpoints (post-/pre-RL) indicates how agentic RL changes teacher models preference on the target token. We find that excluding small fraction of tokens (i.e., with the least 5% RLinduced ).) in the ALFWorld-domain OPD training can effectively mitigate the catastrophic negative transfer on the τ 2 tasks, while maintaining most of the performance gain on ALFWorld tasks. We also extend the analysis to RL-trained GR teacher: selective supervision preserves more CI tool use at the same mean GR accuracy, with reduction in CI accuracy. Figure 1 Agentic OPD can change the ReAct patterns of LLM agents. Our proposed mitigation approach helps alleviate the overfitting to taskspecific patterns. Our key contributions are two-fold: (1) We systematically examine how OPD training, particularly from domain-specialized teachers, changes the reasoning, action, and observation-acquisition patterns of LLM agents across math reasoning (with and without Python code interpreter), ALFWorld, and τ 2-bench. We identifies both positive cross-domain transfer and negative transfer, notably ALF-domain OPD training will drastically make students τ 2 performance drop down; and (2) To mitigate this failure using only ALFsource training trajectories, we propose selecting OPD token positions according to the log-probability change between teacher checkpoint before and after domain-specific RL, excluding the lowest-tail, which largely alleviates the degradation of τ 2 accuracy while maintaining most of the performance gain on the ALFWorld. GR-to-CI extension examines whether the method also preserves mathematical tool-use behavior.

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: On-Policy Distillation. Knowledge distillation transfers teacher behavior to students (Hinton et al., 2015). OPD supervises student-generated contexts (Agarwal et al., 2024; Song and Zheng, 2026), while multiteacher OPD integrates domain experts (Ma et al., 2026). Recent work explores entropy-aware KL objectives (Jin et al., 2026), OPD optimization geometry (Shen et al., 2026b), and efficient offline distillation (Wu et al., 2026b). For agentic OPD, SEED distills hindsight skills (Wu et al., 2026a), ATOD introduces turn-aware weighting (Tan et al., 2026), and ActFirst-OPD separates action and reasoning (Zheng et al., 2026). Studies further examine teacherstudent mismatch in multi-turn agents (Wang et al., 2026b; Zhong et al., 2026; Zhou et al., 2026) and cross-domain transfer (Li et al., 2026; Wang et al., 2026a). Delta-based distillation leverages teacherpredecessor preference differences (Heo et al., 2026). We examine these effects in agentic trajectories (Shen et al., 2026a), tracing solution routes, responses to feedback, and the timing of information requests. This behavioral focus complements work on forgetting (Kirkpatrick et al., 2017; Lopez-Paz and Ranzato, 2017) and multi-task interference (Yu et al., 2020). LLM Agents ReAct Patterns. ReAct couples reasoning with actions and observations (Yao et al., 2022); Toolformer and ToolLLM develop tool-use capabilities (Qin et al., 2024; Schick et al., 2023), and APIBank evaluates tool-augmented interaction (Li et al., 2023). Reasoning methods influence the route to an answer through intermediate derivations and sampled solutions (Wei et al., 2022; Kojima et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2022; Xu et al., 2025). Dynamic reasoning strategies (Aoki et al., 2024) and feedbackbased revision (Shinn et al., 2023) likewise make process behavior important. Our comparisons ask how such observable patterns change after domain distillation, including when improved answer accuracy 2 accompanies less tool use and when frequent actions bypass necessary user feedback. Tool uncertainty (Liu et al., 2024a), procedurally generated environments (Sullivan et al., 2025), and prompt-injection evaluation (Debenedetti et al., 2024) address complementary aspects of reliable interaction.

sections.title: 4 Agentic OPD Reshapes ReAct Patterns
sections.content: We train students with OPD on individual task domains and with MOPD on mixtures of two or three domains, then evaluate each student across tool-enabled and no-tool mathematics, ALFWorld, and τ 2bench. Figure 2 shows that training on one task can substantially change performance on other tasks. For example, CI-only OPD observably raises ALFWorld accuracy from 0.129 to 0.402 (+0.273) and τ 2 accuracy from 0.415 to 0.510 (+0.095). ALF-only OPD instead drastically lowers τ 2 accuracy from 0.415 to 0.066 (0.349). The effects of domain-specific supervision therefore extend beyond the task that supplies its training trajectories, with different outcomes across sourcetarget pairs. Task scores establish the scope of this cross-domain effect but do not show what changed in the students interaction policy. We examine two observable ReAct patterns in the resulting trajectories. First, OPD can shift the route to mathematical answer between tool-assisted computation and direct naturallanguage reasoning ( 4.1). Second, it can change how the student chooses actions, adjusts them after environment feedback, and waits for information or authorization before acting ( 4.2). These analyses connect the performance differences in Figure 2 to specific decisions in the agents reasoning and interaction process.

sections.title: 4.3 Task-matched supervision in MOPD
sections.content: The pronounced shifts above arise after single-source training; MOPD tests whether adding supervision from the evaluated task domain changes these observations. Table 4 compares four pairwise compositions and the three-teacher student through scores and conversational behavior. (1) In mathematics, CI+GR reaches 51.3% accuracy with 74.4% tool attempts when tools are available, while achieving 44.5% accuracy in the no-tool setting. This joint behavior contrasts with GR-only training, which reaches 38.0% accuracy and 14.4% tool attempts in tool-enabled mathematics. The route shift observed after GR-only supervision is thus not fixed when CI supervision is also present. (2) Adding τ 2 prompts and their specialist teacher to ALF training raises τ 2 accuracy from the ALF-only students 0.066 to 0.689. Same-turn askcall co-occurrence falls from 94.3% to 0.24%, and the reviewed ALF+τ 2 rollouts contain no current-request dependency violations. At the same time, ALFWorld accuracy remains high (0.834 versus 0.855 for ALF-only). sections.title: 5 Exploring Mitigations for Negative Transfer in Agentic OPD
sections.content: In this section, we mainly explore how to mitigate the potential cross-task negative transfer in agentic OPD training, using ALF-to-τ 2 transfer ( 4.2) as the main case and extending the analysis to GR-to-CI transfer.

For this extension, we train Qwen3-30B-A3B teacher with tool-free GR reinforcement learning and use its pre-RL checkpoint as the reference. This teacher is distinct from the GR teacher in the earlier cross-domain matrix. Starting from the same 4B student initialization, Full OPD and signedTop95 use the same tool-free training data and are evaluated after 20 updates. sections.title: 6 Conclusion
sections.content: Agentic OPD reshapes how LLM agents reason, act, and obtain observations across domains, producing positive and negative transfer. Task-matched MOPD mitigates the conversational failures induced by ALF supervision on τ 2. As source-only training exploration, we select ordinary OPD supervision po9 sitions using pre/post-domain-RL preference changes. Excluding the lowtail substantially alleviates negative transfer while sacrificing source-domain performance. Token-level analysis reveals concentrated context-dependent suppressive feedback, including reasoning and tool-call onsets. Structural masks, negative masking, and alternative ranking rules yield different sourcetarget trade-offs; none of the reported alternatives reproduces the same target-interaction preservation as signedTop95 in the ALF comparison. An extension with RL-trained GR teacher preserves more CI tool use at equal mean GR accuracy. These findings highlight the importance of controlling where specialization feedback is applied in agentic OPD.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.content: Our experiments focus on the Qwen3 model family with 4B students and mathematical and interactive tasks. Extending the analysis to larger students, other model families, and broader range of agent environments would help establish the generality of the observed transfer patterns. The effects of supervision selection may also depend on the training recipe and interaction protocol, motivating further study across additional configurations.

sections.title: Ethical Considerations
sections.content: This research helps identify potential risks arising when specialized training changes an agents interaction In particular, changes in information gathering and user confirmation can lead to actions behavior. based on unsupported assumptions or actions taken before authorization is obtained. Our findings can inform evaluations of tool-using agents and encourage attention to feedback dependencies, confirmation requirements, and execution permissions in practical applications.

sections.title: A Discussion
sections.content: What should agentic training evaluate? Task accuracy, action content, and feedback dependencies capture different properties of agent behavior. The mathematical results pair improved accuracy with fewer tool attempts; CI transfer pairs better outcomes with action adjustment and query coverage. Conversely, ALF transfer produces request-like text alongside tool calls, some of which depend on user information or authorization not yet obtained. Evaluation should therefore measure how an agent prepares an action, acquires its prerequisites, and responds to the resulting observation, alongside task utility (Arabzadeh et al., 2024) and benchmark breadth (Liu et al., 2024b; Zhou et al., 2024). Importantly, askcall co-occurrence captures generated output patterns rather than actual user requests, and should be interpreted alongside dependency violations and task accuracy. How should supervision be composed? MOPD provides complementary training coverage: CI supports mathematical tool use and feedback-driven actions, while task-matched τ 2 supervision mitigates failures to wait for required user information. These findings connect teacher composition to behavioral coverage and task grouping (Yu et al., 2020; Standley et al., 2020). Source-only -guided selection offers another approach when target-domain training data are unavailable. Excluding small lowtail reduces concentrated suppressive feedback at context-dependent positions, with source-learning trade-off. Delimiter masking, full-block masking, and negative masking fail to reproduce the same sourcetarget balance. These results highlight the importance of feedback location and direction, while further controlled interventions are needed to isolate the mechanisms underlying cross-domain transfer.

sections.title: C Evaluation Protocols and Behavioral Metrics
sections.content: C.1 Evaluation Data and Execution Mathematical evaluation contains 30 AIME2026 (Zhang and Math-AI Team, 2026) questions sampled 16 times and 100 BeyondAIME (ByteDance-Seed, 2025) questions sampled five times, giving 980 trajectories per model. The tool-enabled setting provides code_interpreter; the no-tool setting evaluates textbased solutions. ALFWorld evaluation contains 140 in-distribution and 134 out-of-distribution tasks, each evaluated four times, yielding 1,096 trajectories per model. The τ 2 evaluation contains 100 tasks sampled eight times: 160 airline, 320 retail, and 320 telecom trajectories. We use the same sampling settings for all training rollouts and evaluations: temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, and unrestricted top-k. Teacher token scoring computes probabilities for student-generated tokens at temperature 1.0, without generating additional responses. Agent execution uses the Qwen3 chat template and structured tool calls. The loop parses the complete assistant output before choosing the next interaction branch. In τ 2, exactly one parsed call with objectvalued arguments is submitted to the environment. If prose accompanies the call, it remains in the agent history but is not sent to the customer.
